messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Esperanto, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Return ONLY the table: no notes, no headings, no bullet points, no extra lines.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | Nel | “in the middle of” – locative phrase introducing the position | Use preposition **en** + noun **mezo** + preposition **de**; no comparative ordering; back‑translation check: “Midway upon” | | mezzo | The exact middle point of a journey | Render as noun **mezo** with definite article **la**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “midway” | | del | Genitive marker linking *cammin* to *vita* | Use preposition **de** after **mezo**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “of the” | | cammin | The path or journey being travelled | Translate as **vojo** (road) with definite article **la**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “road” | | di | Preposition marking possession/association (“our life”) | Use preposition **de** after **vojo**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “of” | | nostra | Indicates that the life belongs to the speaker and companions | Translate as possessive adjective **nia**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “our” | | vita | The span of existence of the speaker and companions | Translate as **vivo**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “life” | | mi | Reflexive pronoun marking the experiencer of the action | Use reflexive pronoun **mi** as object of **troviĝi**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “I” | | ritrovai | “I found myself” – self‑locating action | Render with verb **troviĝi** in past tense (**troviĝis**); no comparative; back‑translation check: “found” | | per | Preposition introducing the spatial domain of the finding | Use preposition **en** (or **ĉe**) with accusative **selvon**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “within” | | una | Marks the noun *selva* as non‑specific | Use indefinite article sense via **ioma** or simply **a** omitted; no comparative; back‑translation check: “a” | | selva | A forest, the dark environment | Translate as **arbaro** or **arbo**; use accusative **arbon**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “wood” | | oscura | Qualifies *selva* as lacking light | Translate as adjective **malhela** agreeing in case (**malhelan**); no comparative; back‑translation check: “dark” | | ché | Conjunction introducing the causal clause | Use conjunction **ĉar**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “for” | | la | Definite article specifying the particular *via* | Esperanto omits articles; rely on context; no comparative; back‑translation check: “the” | | diritta | Describes the *via* as the correct/straight one | Translate as adjective **rekta** agreeing in case (**rektan**); no comparative; back‑translation check: “right” | | via | The correct path that should be followed | Translate as **vojo** with accusative **vojon**; no comparative; back‑translation check: “way” | | era | Copular verb indicating a past state | Use past tense of **esti** (**estis**); no comparative; back‑translation check: “had been” | | smarrita | State of being lost; the way is not found | Translate as adjective **perdita** agreeing in case (**perditan**); no comparative; back‑translation check: “missed” |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 1: en la mezo de la vojo de nia vivo / meze de nia vivo vojo / mezo de nia vivo vojo - Line 2: mi trovis min en malluma arbaro / mi troviĝis en malluma arbaro / mi trovis min en malluma arbo - Line 3: ĉar la rekta vojo estis perdita / ĉar rekta vojo estis perdita / ĉar la rekta vojo mankis

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into Esperanto lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Avoid flat modifier stacking: make intended attachment/roles explicit using available function-words/morphology. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

Source Line: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita Line Inventory: - en la mezo de la vojo de nia vivo Assembly Notes: - none (phrase used as‑is) Target Text: en la mezo de la vojo de nia vivo
Source Line: mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, Line Inventory: - mi troviĝas en malluma arbaro Assembly Notes: - none (phrase used as‑is) Target Text: mi troviĝas en malluma arbaro,
Source Line: ché la diritta via era smarrita. Line Inventory: - ĉar la rekta vojo estis perdita Assembly Notes: - none (phrase used as‑as) Target Text: ĉar la rekta vojo estis perdita.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Meaning Drift includes wrong modifier attachment/scope. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line #1 Target Text: en la mezo de la vojo de nia vivo Back-Translation: in the middle of the road of our life Reference Translation: Midway upon the road of our life Checks: End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text:
- Line #2 Target Text: mi troviĝas en malluma arbaro, Back-Translation: I find myself in a dark forest, Reference Translation: I found myself within a dark wood, Checks: End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift FAIL, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text: mi troviĝis en malluma arbaro,
- Line #3 Target Text: ĉar la rekta vojo estis perdita. Back-Translation: because the straight way was lost. Reference Translation: for the right way had been missed. Checks: End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text:
``` en la mezo de la vojo de nia vivo mi troviĝis en malluma arbaro, ĉar la rekta vojo estis perdita. ```
